TESTIMONY BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON AGRICULTURE, CONSERVATION AND FORESTRY
IN SUPPORT OF LD 1528

An Act to Support Farmland Conservation

April 17, 2025

Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry, my name is Craig Lapine, and I am the Director of the
Bureau of Agriculture, Food and Rural Resources (BAF RR) within the Maine Department of
Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF). I am speaking in favor of LD 1528, An Act to
Support Farmland Conservation.
LD 1528 aims to enhance and strengthen the Working Farmland Access and Protection Program (WFAPP), which resides in BAFRR, to better support farmland conservation in Maine. It does
this primarily by creating a dedicated Resource Management Coordinator within the Bureau, by
effecting an administrative change by establishing a WFAPP account within the Bureau----a
change that opens the door for new flexibility and creativity in how we approach farmland
protection, and by capitalizing that account with a one-time, non-lapsing allocation of $1 million.
While the WFAPP account language was included in the Governor's budget proposal, the
funding allocation and staff position was not. Should the proposed position and allocation in this
bill not be fiinded at this time, creation of the WFAPP account within BAFRR is still important
to the Department, as we anticipate opportunities to pursue other sources of funding that could
seed this account and serve to accelerate fannland conservation in Maine.
The benefits of farms and farmland to our state and its people are numerous, from providing local and regional food security to economic, cultural, environmental, and educational benefits,
aesthetic values, and critical wildlife habitat. The Maine Climate Action Plan, Maine Won 't Wait (MWW), recommends that 30% of our natural and working lands in Maine be conserved by 2030 and that Maine-produced food consumption be increased to 30% by 2030. While we currently count 22% of such lands as conserved, most of the land in that figure is working
forestland and recreational lands. Approximately 3.6% of our farmland is protected at this time,
which lags far behind most other states in the Northeast. MWW also points out that there has

Testimony before the Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry By Eliza Paterson, American Farmland Trust, Senior New England Policy Associate April 17th, 2025
RE: Support for LD 1528 - An Act to Support Farmland Conservation
Dear Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and esteemed members of the Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry,
Thank you for the opportunity to submit testimony in support of LD 1528.
My name is Eliza Paterson, and I am American Farmland Trust's (AFT's) Senior New England Policy Associate. AFT is the nation's leading conservation organization dedicated to protecting farmland, promoting sound farming practices, and keeping farmers on the land. Established in 1985, AFT's New England Program works to save the land that sustains us across the region. AFT has a long history of working in Maine, stemming back to supporting the first farmland protection projects undertaken through the Land for Maine's Future program.
Farmland plays a vital role in the state's economy, rural communities and food security - and is regionally important. LD 1528 would increase the ability of the state to protect this vital resource by creating an account managed by the Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF)'s Bureau of Agriculture, Food, and Rural Resources to facilitate an expansion of publicly funded farmland protection efforts, building staff capacity within this existing state program, and increasing public funding for farmland conservation through a $1 million appropriation.
Maine's farmland is at risk. According to the 2022 Census of Agriculture, between 2017 and 2022, more than 82,000 acres of farmland in Maine fell out of agricultural production. At the same time, Maine has protected less than five percent of the state's farmland to date - the lowest percentage of any New England state.
Protecting farmland through agricultural conservation easements keeps land available for agricultural use and creates more affordable access to farmland for both new and established farmers. This supports a thriving agricultural economy in Maine, which is essential for rural economic development, the viability of farm businesses, maintaining agricultural land in production, and ensuring a resilient food system.
Maine needs to pursue different strategies simultaneously to accelerate farmland conservation efforts. These strategies include continued funding for the Land for Maine's Future Program, specific funding for farmland conservation, and promoting farm viability. And because Maine has the most agricultural land of any of the six New England states by far, as well as the largest amount of prime and important farmland, protecting Maine farmland is important to the region's food system and food security.

LD 1528 provides dedicated public funding to protect working farmland and will help ensure that the state has the program structures and capacity in place for efficient use of this funding through increased staff, and expansion of public funding, and $1 million in appropriations.
Moreover, LD 1528 aligns with the 2024 Maine Won't Wait climate action plan, which establishes new targets specific to farmland protection. This calls for the state to secure ongoing funding dedicated to farmland protection and to double the amount of permanently protected farmland by 2030.
As a national and regional leader in farmland protection, we fully support this legislation and urge the committee to pass it this session. If you have any questions, please feel free to reach out to me at epaterson@farmland.org or Jim Habana Hafner, Ph.D., AFT New England's Regional Director, at jhafner@farmland.org.
On behalf of AFT, thank you for your time and for the opportunity to submit testimony in support of LD 1528.
Sincerely,
Eliza Paterson Senior New England Policy Associate American Farmland Trust
American Farmland Trust is an agricultural non-profit organization with a mission to save the land that sustains us by protecting farmland, promoting sound farming practices, and keeping farmers on the land. AFT is the only
national agricultural organization that approaches its work in this comprehensive, holistic manner. We recognize the connection between the land, forward-looking farming practices, and the farmers who do the work.

Testimony of the Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association in support of
LD 1528 - An Act to Support Farmland Conservation April 16, 2025
Good afternoon Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry. My name is Heather Spalding and I am deputy director of the Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association (MOFGA). Thank you for the opportunity to advocate for LD 1528 - An Act to Support Farmland Conservation.
A broad-based community, MOFGA is transforming our food system by supporting farmers, empowering people to feed their communities, and advocating for an organic future. MOFGA certifies 537 organic farms and processing operations representing more than $120 million in sales. We're working hard to create opportunities for Maine's next generation of farmers. Each of these farmers is a Maine businessperson for whom economic health and environmental health are interdependent. While MOFGA envisions a future of healthy ecosystems, communities, people, and economies sustained by the practices of organic agriculture, we attribute our success to collaboration and outreach to growers across the management spectrum.
Last year during the 131st Legislature, MOFGA supported a bill (LD 579) similar to LD 1528 before you today. LD 1528 would do three things:
� Create an account managed by the Bureau of Agriculture, Food, and Rural Resources to facilitate a rapid expansion of publicly funded farmland protection efforts;
� Build staff capacity within this existing state program so it can function as intended when created by the Legislature by establishing one Resource Management Coordinator position; and
� Increase public funding for farmland conservation through a $1 million appropriation from the General Fund -- the appropriation being the main difference from the last Legislature's bill on this subject.
MOFGA supports LD 1528 because Maine's farmland is precious and finite, and it's a critical aspect of a food system that is healthy and fair for all. The 2022 Census of Agriculture reported that between 2017 and 2022, Maine lost more than 6% of its productive farmland, saw a per-acre farmland cost increase of 44%, and a cost of farm production increase of 25%. Maine Farmland Trust reports that Maine is way behind other states in the Northeast when it comes to farmland preservation. Maine has about 60,000 acres of protected land (less than 5% of Maine farmland) compared to Massachusetts with about 75,000, New York with about 120,000, Vermont with 173,000, New Jersey with 247,000, and Pennsylvania with more than 650,000. Similarly, Maine is way behind all of these states with farmland protection funding.
Increasing Maine's farm conservation easements will help move Maine toward the climate action plan goals of conserving 30% of Maine land by 2030, and increasing the amount of food produced and consumed in Maine to 30% by 2030. We understand that Maine currently relies on producers outside of the state for about 96% of the food we consume though we have the soils, the water, the climate and the know-how to produce a healthy, diverse and delicious diet. Farmland preservation is essential if we are going to increase our selfreliance in the food and agriculture system. LD 1528 would help Maine ensure a land base with continuously improved soil quality in order to have a thriving and resilient agricultural economy that provides a nutritious and delicious diet for all people in Maine and many beyond.
We urge you to support this legislation and we appreciate your consideration.

Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and esteemed members of the Joint
Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry: I am Senator Rick
Bennett of Oxford, and I have the honor of serving 14 communities in Western Maine in
the State Senate. I am proud to sponsor LD 1528, "An Act to Support Farmland
Conservation."
Maine's farmland is the bedrock of our rural economy, our food system, and our cultural
heritage. If we are serious about supporting agriculture in this state--and I believe we
are--~we must be equally serious about protecting the very land that makes it all possible.
The 2022 Census of Agriculture makes clear what many of us have seen happening on the ground: between 2017 and 2022, Maine lost more than 82,000 acres of farmland.
That's an alarming trend, driven by increasing development pressure, non-farming land
buyers, and land prices that are out of reach for too many farmers.
Today, less than 5% of Maine's farmland is permanently protected--making us last in New England on this front. That is simply unacceptable if we're aiming to build a
resilient and thriving agricultural economy. Conservation easements are one proven tool. They not only preserve farmland for future generations, but they can also make it more affordable for young and beginning farmers to gain access to land.
LD 1528 is a smart, targeted measure that directly supports the goals outlined in our updated Maine Won't Wait climate action plan. That plan calls for doubling protected farmland by 2030 and ensuring no net loss. To achieve that, we must act decisive1y--and
this bill helps us do just that.
Specifically, LD 1528 would:
- Create a dedicated account within the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry to expand publicly funded farmland protection;
- Establish a Resource Management Coordinator position to build much-needed capacity; and
- Provide a $1 million appropriation to increase direct investment in farmland
protection.

Testimony of Shelley Megquier, Policy & Research Director, Maine Farmland Trust, to the 132""
Legislature's Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry April 17, 2025
Good afternoon Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry. My name is Shelley Megquier and I am the Policy & Research Director at Maine Farmland Trust (MFT). I am providing testimony on behalf of MFT in
support of LD 1528--An Act to Support Farm/and Conservation.
MFT is a member-powered statewide organization that works to protect farmland, support farmers, and
advance the future of farming. Our goals are to keep agricultural lands working and help farmers and
their communities thrive. Since our founding in 1999, MFT has helped to permanently protect farmland
in every county in Maine, amounting to nearly 57,000 acres across 345 farms. Our Farm Network includes more than 550 farms that have participated in MFT's programming either through an agricultural easement or through one of our programs. Our main program areas are Farmland Protection, Farmland Access, Stewardship, Farm Business Planning, PFAS Support, Climate Resilience, and Policy and Research.
Protecting farmland is critical for ensuring we have the land base needed to grow our agricultural economy and strengthen food security for our communities, state, and region. But, farmland in Maine is at risk. The 2022 Census of Agriculture showed that between 2017 and 2022, more than 82,000 acres of
farmland in Maine fell out of agricultural production? Farmland in Maine is being lost to agriculture due to increasing development pressures, a growing interest in farmland from non-farming buyers, dramatic increases in the cost of land, and farm viability challenges that are making it harder for farmers to afford to keep their land in agriculture. At the same time, less than 5 percent of Maine's farmland is currently
protected through an agricultural conservation easement --- the best estimate we have is "'3.5% and this is the lowest amount of any state in New England. Protecting farmland through a conservation easement keeps land available for agricultural use and creates more affordable access to farmland for both new and established farmers.
Agricultural conservation also helps to build resilience to climate change for our state and communities.
in fact, the state's updated 2024 climate action plan Maine Won't Wait establishes new targets specific to farmland protection -- calling for Maine to secure and commit ongoing, dedicated funding for farmland conservation to double the amount of permanently protected farmland in the state by 2030 and ensure no net loss of farmland in Maine. In order to realize this goal, we need to meet the rapid
growth in development pressure across the state with an equally rapid expansion of our farmland protection efforts, especially publicly funded farmland protection.
The Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) Bureau of Agriculture, Food and Rural Resources' Working Farmland Access and Protection Program (WFAPP) is a perfect vehicle for dedicated funding to farmland conservation, as it is designed to protect Maine's most productive and economically significant farmland. This language in this bill reiterates language that was put forth in the Governor's
biennial budget to ensure that WFAPP can receive dedicated funding.
